## Cross-panel ghost interpolation (`interpolate`) {#sec-ch03-csinterp}

<!-- PROVENANCE

Across a panel edge the two panels' coordinate lines meet at an angle, so a ghost cannot be a copy of a neighbour's
cell. snapy fills each ghost by one-dimensional linear interpolation along the shared edge, from a strip of the
neighbour's cells. The source of a ghost in layer $\ell$ does not sit opposite it: it slides along the edge toward the
edge midpoint by up to $n_g - \tfrac12$ cells, independently of resolution. So the strip is widened by $n_g$ cells on
each side, and when a panel is split among blocks the widened strip reaches into the sender's own intra-panel halo,
which must be current; the sync therefore runs in two phases, intra-panel first. Velocities are rotated from the
sender's panel frame to the global spherical $(r, \theta, \varphi)$ frame before sending and back into the receiver's
frame after interpolation.

Edges and corners have different accuracy: the along-edge linear interpolation is second order in the
source abscissa, but after both exchange phases `fill_corners` synthesises each $x_2$-$x_3$ corner as the mean
of the two adjacent ghost strips. That corner fill is exact on constants and only first order for a field
with a gradient, because the sampled strip cells are displaced from the corner cell. See @sec-ch03-exchange
for the construction, @eq-ch03-exchange-corner and its error check
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::fill_corners >}}).

Local symbols: $\ell = 1..n_g$ the ghost layer counted from the panel edge (count);
$N_{\mathrm{p}}$ the cells along a panel edge, $n_2 n_{\mathrm b,2}$ (count); $\Delta\xi = \pi/(2N_{\mathrm{p}})$ the angular cell
width [rad]; $u$ the fractional source abscissa along the edge, in cells of the source panel [-]; $\eta'$ the
along-edge angle of a ghost centre on the source panel [rad]; $a_\ell = (\ell - \tfrac12)\Delta\xi$ the angular distance
of a layer-$\ell$ ghost centre past the edge [rad].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** A ghost across a panel edge is a linear interpolation along the edge at an abscissa precomputed by mapping
the ghost centre onto the neighbouring panel (@eq-ch03-csinterp-weights); velocities travel in the global spherical
frame.

**Data.** In: the neighbour panel's interior cells and the stored source abscissae `usrc_LR`, `usrc_BT`. Out: the
edge ghost cells, in the units of the synced variables.

**Placement.** Abscissae at setup (`reset`); interpolation in each sync that asks for it.

**Activation.** `SyncOptions.interpolate(true)`, set by the per-stage conserved sync, the initial primitive sync and
the scalar syncs; off for face states and the donor factor. Requires `interp_order: 2`; a subdivided panel
($n_{\mathrm b,2} > 1$) runs the sync in two phases.

**Guarantee / limits.** Second order (linear interpolation) in the along-edge abscissa.

**Evidence.** `test_cubed_sphere_exchange`, `test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python`, `test_exchange`;
check `[C11]`; the ctest entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

### Derivation

The slide follows from the gnomonic map, as in `sources/canoe__cubedsphere_decomposition_TECH_REPORT.md` §1. Take the
right edge of a panel, $\xi = \pi/4$. A ghost of layer $\ell$ sits at $\xi = \pi/4 + (\ell - \tfrac12)\Delta\xi$ and
along-edge angle $\eta$; its direction is $(1, \tan\xi, \tan\eta)$ in the panel's frame. Take the panel to be +X,
whose points are $(1, a, b)$ in global Cartesian components; its right neighbour is +Y, whose points are $(-a', 1, b')$
({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_constants.h cs_face_xyz_from_tan >}}). The +Y frame is the +X frame turned by $\pi/2$
about the $z$[^rg-cd186f5447b7] axis, which the four equatorial panels share; the edge itself is the line $x = y$. In three steps:

1. The ghost direction is $(1, \tan\xi, \tan\eta)$ in global components.
2. In the +Y frame (normal $y$, along-$a'$ direction $-x$, along-$b'$ direction $z$) it reads $(\tan\xi, -1, \tan\eta)$.
3. Dividing by the normal component gives $(1, -1/\tan\xi, \tan\eta/\tan\xi)$, so $\tan\xi' = -1/\tan\xi$ and the
   along-edge angle is

$$
\tan\eta' = \frac{\tan\eta}{\tan\xi}.
$$ {#eq-ch03-csinterp-slide}

On the edge itself $\tan\xi = 1$ and $\eta' = \eta$. Outside it the ghost sits at $\xi = \pi/4 + a_\ell$, and to first
order in $a_\ell$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tan\xi &= \frac{1 + \tan a_\ell}{1 - \tan a_\ell} = 1 + 2a_\ell + O(a_\ell^2), \\
\tan\eta' &= \frac{\tan\eta}{\tan\xi} = \tan\eta\,(1 - 2a_\ell) + O(a_\ell^2), \\
\eta' - \eta &= \frac{\tan\eta' - \tan\eta}{1 + \tan^2\eta} + O(a_\ell^2)
 = -2a_\ell\sin\eta\cos\eta + O(a_\ell^2) = -a_\ell\sin 2\eta + O(a_\ell^2),
\end{aligned}
$$

the third line using $\mathrm{d}\eta/\mathrm{d}\tan\eta = \cos^2\eta = 1/(1 + \tan^2\eta)$. This is a slide of
$(\ell - \tfrac12)\sin 2\eta$ cells toward $\eta = 0$, at most $n_g - \tfrac12$ cells, at the corners. The code does not use the expansion: `cs_build_ghost_usrc` maps each ghost centre through Cartesian
coordinates onto the source panel and converts the angle to a cell abscissa $u = (\eta' + \pi/4)/\Delta\xi - \tfrac12$,
reversed when the edge table says so ({{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_build_ghost_usrc >}}). The ghost value is then

$$
q_{\mathrm{ghost}} = (1 - w)\,q_{\lfloor u\rfloor} + w\,q_{\lfloor u\rfloor + 1}, \qquad w = u - \lfloor u\rfloor,
$$ {#eq-ch03-csinterp-weights}

with the cell index shifted by an integer per block. @eq-ch03-csinterp-weights is the `interp_order == 2` branch of
`_interp_ghost_LR` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::_interp_ghost_LR >}}) and of `_interp_ghost_BT`
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::_interp_ghost_BT >}}). Linear interpolation is exact for linear data and has an $O(\Delta\xi^2)$
error otherwise. The margin is the largest slide rounded up, $\lceil n_g - \tfrac12\rceil = n_g$, which is
`cs_interp_margin` ({{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.hpp cs_interp_margin >}}). For $N_{\mathrm{p}} = 64$ and $n_g = 3$ the exact slide
from @eq-ch03-csinterp-slide is at most 2.4955 cells and departs from the expansion by at most 0.072 cells
(`[C11]`).[^csi-c11]

[^csi-c11]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C11]`; a numpy port of the ghost-source positions of `src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp` at the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

The ordering constraint is derived in the same source, §5 and §6: on a subdivided panel the widened strip packed for a
cross-panel neighbour contains cells this block holds only as intra-panel ghosts, and those are written by the unpack
of the same sync. One round cannot satisfy that, so the intra-panel round completes first.

### Numerical method

The abscissae are built once in `reset` for the whole edge (face 0, left side, reused for every edge by symmetry) and
kept as a double per ghost; the block's offset into the edge is kept as a separate integer and added to the index after
`floor`, so the stored weight does not depend on the decomposition. A sync with interpolation on a cubed sphere with
$n_{\mathrm b,2} > 1$ or $n_{\mathrm b,3} > 1$ runs as intra-panel (no interpolation), then cross-panel, then `fill_corners`. In the
cross-panel pack the strip is widened by the margin, its velocities are rotated to the spherical frame (conserved
momenta are raised to contravariant first), and the strip is relabelled for the neighbour's orientation by the
reverse, flip and transpose flags. In the unpack the wide strip lands in the ghost zone and its margin, the ghost is
interpolated from it while all of it is still in the spherical frame, and only the narrow ghost zone is rotated into
the receiver's frame (and lowered back to covariant for conserved momenta). @fig-ch03-csinterp-slide shows the slide.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-csinterp-slide
#| fig-cap: "Two panels meeting at an edge (thick line). Ghost centres of layers $\\ell = 1, 2, 3$ beyond the edge (open circles) and the points of the neighbouring panel they are interpolated from (filled circles), joined by arrows: the sources slide along the edge toward its midpoint, most at the panel corners. Computed from @eq-ch03-csinterp-slide for $N_{\\mathrm{p}} = 16$ cells per edge; both axes are in cells."
#| fig-alt: "Ghost centres in three rows beside a vertical edge, each connected to a source point shifted toward the middle of the edge."
#| echo: false
```

: Code map of the cross-panel interpolation. {#tbl-ch03-csinterp-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-csinterp-code):

1. At setup `reset` calls `cs_build_ghost_usrc` for the whole edge and stores the block's slice with the integer
   shift `usrc_shift_LR` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::reset >}}).
2. `exchange` splits an interpolating sync on a subdivided panel into `intra_panel_only` and `cross_panel_only`
   rounds and calls `fill_corners` after both ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange >}}).
3. `serialize` returns after the intra-panel neighbours in phase 1; in phase 2 it widens the strip with `extend_x2`
   or `extend_x3` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}}), sets `rev_flag`, `trans_flag` and `flip_flag`
   ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}}), rotates the velocities with `cs_apply_velocity_transform_`
   ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}}) and relabels the strip with `flip_out`
   ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::serialize >}}).
4. `deserialize` lands the wide strip with `sub_w`, calls `interp_ghost`, then rotates the narrow ghost zone back
   with `cs_apply_velocity_transform_` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize >}}).

**How to use it.** The interpolation is on for a cubed-sphere card (@sec-ch03-gnomonic); the only key is
`geometry.cells.interp_order`, which must be 2 (its default). The margin $\lceil n_g - \tfrac12\rceil = n_g$ needs
no key. Refused: `interp_order` other than 2, with "Only 2nd order ghost interpolation is supported". The linear
branch of @eq-ch03-csinterp-weights and the margin are
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::_interp_ghost_LR >}},
{{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.hpp cs_interp_margin >}}):

```cpp
  auto buf0 = buf.gather(-3, u0.expand(vec));
  auto buf1 = buf.gather(-3, u1.expand(vec));

  if (options->interp_order() == 2) {
    return x * buf1 + (1.0 - x) * buf0;
```

```cpp
inline int cs_interp_margin(int nghost) { return nghost; }
```

: Tests of the cross-panel interpolation. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-csinterp-tests}

The bitwise case is `subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block` ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block >}});
the deck is the card written by `write_card`, $8\times8$ cells per panel, `nb2` = 1, 2 and 4, all $6n_{\mathrm b,2}^2$ blocks in one
process ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp write_card >}}). Its CUDA twin
`subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block_cuda` is in the same binary and skips without a GPU
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block_cuda >}}). The tag case is `rejects_tags_that_collide_with_the_variable_offset`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CommTag.rejects_tags_that_collide_with_the_variable_offset >}}).
The same binary holds the four cases of the radial-wall corner refresh at panel seams, which test the exchange's
caller rather than the interpolation: `custom_noop_callback_identity`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.custom_noop_callback_identity >}}) and the three
`check_radial_halo_refresh` cases, for example `radial_walls_refresh_exchange_owned_horizontal_halos`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.radial_walls_refresh_exchange_owned_horizontal_halos >}});
their deck and assertions are in @sec-ch03-cornerrefresh. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing
evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `interp_order` must be 2; the fourth-order branch of `_interp_ghost_LR` and `_interp_ghost_BT` is unreachable.
- Bitwise decomposition independence is tested for `nb2` = 1, 2, 4 in one process, one stage.
:::

The source report records bit-for-bit agreement of `nb2` = 1, 2 and 4 over one cycle on CPU with gloo and one block
per rank (`sources/canoe__cubedsphere_decomposition_TECH_REPORT.md` §7 and §10); that was measured on a development
build, not at the pin, and re-running it at the pin needs the report's multi-rank gate, which is not committed. The
margin cells of the wide landing zone keep the neighbour's spherical frame after the unpack; the same report shows
with a gate that nothing reads them (§8), which was not re-checked at the pin. `_interpolate_to_local` is a stub with a
TODO and no effect ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::_interpolate_to_local >}}). `DeviceTest.interpolate_LR` sets up linear data
and asserts nothing, as written in `interpolate_LR` ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp DeviceTest.interpolate_LR >}}). The switch combinations
that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
